effect_alone: Before seal: every configuration choice, including profile and mutations (a mutant-* deployment), witness sets and thresholds (for example q=1 of its own key), the relay, authority roots and CA-Admins, policies, record owners and destinations. After seal: nothing.
f_note: Trusted-setup assumption standing in for HMBC's collaborative initial configuration (III-C1, III-E). F must either state it or require every organization to verify the deployment manifest (runtime code hashes, constructor arguments, witness sets) before use; related to D50.

effect_alone: Signs certificates off chain: any GID, roles, serial and validity under Hx. In paper-strict and repaired-e, also the signature its CA-Admin needs to publish Hx lists.
cannot_change: other authorities' lists; the authority set
f_note: A certificate is valid until its own CRL revokes it; no other organization can revoke it.

effect_alone: paper-minimal: publishes any Hx CRL or TempACL alone. paper-strict and repaired-e: needs the Hx root signature. Every accepted update bumps the global authEpoch.
classification: paper-supported behavior (issuer scoping); tested reconstruction result (authEpoch coupling)
f_note: CA-Admin and root normally belong to the same hospital, so the two-key split adds nothing against a faulty hospital.

actor: Faulty hospital Hx (root + CA-Admin + its users; in F also one witness)
fixture_keys: Hx-root + Hx-ca-admin + GIDs it controls (+ one of four witness keys in F)
effect_alone: Grants for its own GIDs to any record whose policy clause accepts Hx-issued roles (fixture emergency policy: Doctor from ANY issuer, OnDuty from the same issuer). Revokes and un-revokes its own credentials. Invalidates every user's in-flight request by updating its lists. Installs lists with any lifetime. In F, one of the four witness signatures.
needs_others_for: two more witnesses for any decision/checkpoint/receipt quorum under q=3
cannot_change: other authorities' lists; the authority set; policies; record owners; a q=3 quorum alone
classification: tested reconstruction result; paper-supported behavior (Rule 2 any-issuer reading)
f_note: A witness quorum does not limit credential issuance: honest witnesses check the same genuinely valid credentials. Per-issuer trust is a residual for the F trust matrix.

fixture_keys: witness-1 (E: sole witness); F: one of four
alone_changes: E (q=1): S24|S25|S29 and, with the relay, S19|S07. F (q=3): none alone
effect_alone: E: installs any checkpoint, including one that blocks the DBC forever; attests decisions for requests never logged on the PBC and for records the PBC never verified; with the relay, records outcomes. F: one signature gives INSUFFICIENT_QUORUM, measured with a test-only 4-witness KSSC at q=3; three signers do install a poison checkpoint.
needs_others_for: F: two more witnesses for any quorum
cannot_change: anything on the PBC except through a relay-submitted receipt
f_note: The DBC checks only quorum signatures and bindings. It neither re-verifies the user's request signature nor the credential records, so F safety rests on honest witnesses checking these themselves (SPEC section 5).

alone_changes: paper: S25|S29 (policyEnf), S19|S07 (reportOutcome). repaired-e: S19|S07 only together with a quorum receipt
effect_alone: paper: grants for any GID and data with asserted attributes, and arbitrary outcome records. repaired-e: withholds or delays outcomes (requests stay visibly pending); cannot forge them.
needs_others_for: repaired-e: a quorum receipt to record an outcome
cannot_change: repaired-e: grants or checkpoints (anyone may submit those with valid signatures)
classification: paper-supported behavior with SPEC_GAP (paper profiles); tested reconstruction result (repaired-e)
f_note: In repaired-e the relay key gates only outcome recording; a faulty relay suppresses all PBC outcome logs (audit availability).

effect_alone: Registers once; requests (each logged); consumes its own nonces through granted requests.
cannot_change: its own recipient key after registration; its registration
f_note: No deregistration path; revocation acts only through the issuer's CRL.

effect_alone: Appends request log entries and denials for any digest. Submits any valid checkpoint or decision certificate it observes (front-running or delaying is possible; REPLAY and nonce checks bound the effect).
needs_others_for: valid signatures for anything beyond logging
cannot_change: grants, checkpoints or outcomes without valid signatures
classification: paper-supported behavior (V-A5 logs every request); tested reconstruction result
f_note: Log growth is bounded only by gas cost.

effect_alone: Ownership matters only for DATA_OWNER clauses. The fixture policy has none, so H2 owning P1 constrains nothing (see A04).
f_note: Under the fixture policy, any single authority's doctor-on-duty reads H2's record. That is the conservative Rule 2 reading, not a defect.

fixture_keys: Anvil node (E); validators in a real deployment
effect_alone: Under a safe-ledger assumption: censors, delays or reorders transactions and chooses block.timestamp within the chain's rules; every expiry and freshness check uses block.timestamp. Without that assumption: any state.
f_note: Core F assumes safe ledgers (SPEC section 5); the F0 matrix should also state a timestamp-skew bound and an eventual-inclusion assumption.

effect_alone: The grant is permission only; a faulty worker releases without or against a grant and the ledger cannot prevent it.
f_note: SPEC section 5 residual: a compromised key worker bypasses a correct quorum.

effect_alone: retrieveLog reverts (F governance placeholder); all logs and events are publicly readable anyway.
classification: paper-supported behavior (Table 2) with an explicit E omission
f_note: Log confidentiality is not achievable on a transparent ledger; F governance can gate only an off-chain service.
